editorial.description_en: Silt at the bottom of standing water — dark, warm, and almost without chroma.
editorial.description_ja: 水の底にたまった泥のような、暗い茶。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.312, C 0.048, h 60.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 泥 (doro, mud) + 底 (soko, bottom). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Mud Bottom" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 泥底. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — furu-gawara at ΔE00 5.5, ame-doro at ΔE00 6.1, do-ma at ΔE00 8.1. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (240°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
